title: Java OOP
learningObjectives: Define object-oriented programming and describe its purpose.
Distinguish a class from an object created from that class.
Identify how objects combine state and behaviour.
Explain how encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism support OOP.
Recognize when an object-based design can model a real problem clearly.

understand.concept: Object-oriented programming (OOP) organizes software around objects. An object combines state, represented by fields, with behaviour, represented by methods. A class defines the structure and behaviour that its objects share. Java supports core OOP ideas including encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction.
understand.whyItMatters: OOP helps represent a problem as cooperating objects with clear responsibilities. It can make larger programs easier to extend, test and maintain when classes have focused roles.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-designed object as a small service with a clear responsibility: it keeps the information it owns and exposes only the operations other code needs.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a design aid; Java access, inheritance and dispatch follow the language's exact rules.

explain.narrative:
## Classes and objects

A class is a blueprint; an object is a particular instance created from that class. Objects can hold different field values while sharing methods.

## Four OOP principles

Encapsulation protects an object's internal state. Inheritance lets a class derive from another class. Polymorphism lets one parent type refer to different child objects and dispatch overridden methods. Abstraction exposes essential operations while hiding implementation detail.

## Design with responsibilities

Prefer classes with cohesive data and behaviour. Avoid creating classes that merely wrap one value without adding useful responsibility.

## Common mistakes

- Calling a class and an object the same thing.
- Treating inheritance as the only way to reuse code.
- Exposing every field publicly.
- Creating overly large classes with unrelated responsibilities.

examples.title: Model a simple object
examples.code:
class Lamp { boolean on; void turnOn() { on = true; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Lamp lamp = new Lamp(); lamp.turnOn(); System.out.println(lamp.on); } }
examples.explanation: The object stores state and exposes a method that changes it.

examples.title: Create two independent objects
examples.code:
class Counter { int value; }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Counter a = new Counter(); Counter b = new Counter(); a.value = 3; b.value = 8; System.out.println(a.value + b.value); } }
examples.explanation: Each object has its own instance field value.

examples.title: Combine state and behaviour
examples.code:
class Fan { int speed; void setSpeed(int next) { speed = next; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Fan fan = new Fan(); fan.setSpeed(2); System.out.println(fan.speed); } }
examples.explanation: The Fan object keeps a speed value and changes it through behaviour.

examples.title: Use a class as a type
examples.code:
class Book { String title; }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Book book = new Book(); book.title = "Java"; System.out.println(book.title); } }
examples.explanation: The variable book refers to an object whose type is Book.

examples.title: Objects collaborate through methods
examples.explanation: One object uses another object's public behaviour to complete a task.

questions.prompt: What is an object in Java?
questions.explanation: An object is created from a class definition.

questions.prompt: Which OOP feature protects internal state through controlled access?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation controls how object state is accessed or changed.

questions.prompt: What does a class primarily define?
questions.answer: A structure and behaviour for its objects
options: A structure and behaviour for its objects
questions.explanation: A class describes the fields and methods its instances can have.

questions.prompt: Which OOP principle supports one parent type referring to different child objects?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism allows a common type to represent different implementations.

questions.prompt: What is a useful object-oriented design goal?
questions.answer: Give each class a clear, cohesive responsibility
options: Give each class a clear, cohesive responsibility
Put every operation in one class
questions.explanation: Focused classes are easier to understand and maintain.
